The Laundry Room Waltz
One quarter buys nine minutes of dryer. They keep buying more.
A restaurant manager and a night cab driver only ever meet for one nine-minute dryer cycle. The trick is getting out of the basement.

Dev manages a busy bistro and talks through every silence; Arthur drives a cab at night and likes the silence just fine. A red sock turns Dev's only white shirt pink, and suddenly Tuesdays at 9:40 mean something in the basement of 418 Linden. You decide whether Dev keeps inventing a sad story for the quiet man across the folding table, or asks what's actually outside the nine minutes.
A third-floor neighbor who also does laundry on Tuesdays, and has definitely noticed.
If nobody asks, they'll spend years being nine minutes of each other's week and call it enough.
